text:
Fix applied. Verifying against all test cases by tracing the logic:

- `wrap("the quick brown fox", 10)`: "the quick" (9 ≤ 10) → "brown" doesn't fit (15 > 10) → new line "brown fox" (9 ≤ 10) → `["the quick", "brown fox"]` ✓
- `wrap("aaa bbb", 7)`: 3+1+3 = 7 ≤ 7 → `["aaa bbb"]` ✓ (the reported bug)
- `wrap("aaa bbb ccc", 7)`: "aaa bbb" fills exactly, "ccc" → 11 > 7 → `["aaa bbb", "ccc"]` ✓
- `wrap("abcdefghij", 4)`: long-word splitting path is untouched → `["abcd", "efgh", "ij"]` ✓

The one-character-short behavior came from the strict `<` in the greedy packing condition; `<=` matches the documented contract ("a line may be exactly `width` long").

arguments.summary: Fixed the off-by-one in wrapper/wrap.py: the greedy line-packing condition used `len(current) + 1 + len(word) < width`, which refused to add a word that would make the line exactly `width` characters long.
